newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down on weak foreign interest.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down on weak foreign interest.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended down on poor foreign participation and weak futures in Tokyo, traders said.
They said the domestic market saw little trading and drifted without leads for most of the day.
One trading house reported buying 500 tonnes of bulk latex at 230 Malaysian cents (91 cents) a kg for delivery between February and April.
A spokesman for the company also said it had purchased 33.6 tonnes of SMR L at 343 cents per kg for prompt delivery to the South Korean market.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licencing Board quoted January RSS1 buyer at 316 cents a kg, down one cent from Tuesday. January SMR 20 buyer was also a cent lower at 304.50.

Trading houses offered the SMR CV at 363 cents, SMR L at 343, SMR 5 at 318, SMR 10 at 307, SMR 20 at 306 and drum latex at 234. Traders said they expect business to be slow through December with most market players going on holiday.
The INRO five-day moving average fell to 242.16 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Dec 3 from 242.44 on Dec 2. The daily indicator price dipped to 241.76 from 242.10.
